text:
aj: Heads up — running into a weird TLS/SNI + redirect issue with the Kotlin client behind our corp proxy. Authorization header gets dropped on redirect and streaming NDJSON chunks look fragmented. Using OkHttp + shaded libs in the fat jar. Anyone seen this combo?

maria: Can you paste the client build and the exact redirect response? Quick guess: OkHttp strips Authorization on cross-host redirects.

aj: Here's the client setup (simplified):
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .proxy(proxy)
  .followRedirects(true)
  .followSslRedirects(true)
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .build()
```
Responses show 307 -> same host but proxy rewrites host header, then auth missing. Also saw: `java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: okhttp3.internal.connection.StreamAllocation.someMethod()` in prod logs after shading.

leo: yep OkHttp intentionally removes Authorization for redirects to a different origin. For 307 it should keep it for same-origin, but proxy-induced host changes can make it look cross-origin. We usually handle by using an `Authenticator` or a network interceptor to reapply the header on redirected requests.

yash: Network interceptor suggestion:
```kotlin
client.newBuilder().addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val req = chain.request()
    .newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", currentToken())
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```
That forces the header even if OkHttp would drop it.

maria: Also investigate the shading error — NoSuchMethodError often means mixed okhttp versions or relocation issues in the shadow jar. Run `jar tf app.jar | grep okhttp3` and `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath | grep okhttp` to confirm.

aj: Ran `jar tf` — I see both `okhttp3` and relocated `com.mycompany.shadow.okhttp3` packages. We do a shadowRelocate for some libs but not consistent. Stack shows: `NoSuchMethodError: okhttp3.Authenticator.authenticate` at runtime.

deploy-bot: FYI, runtime patch 2026-01-30 adjusted header handling in okhttp3 4.11.x — might be related if you're pulling that version.

leo: For the shading: prefer relocating all okhttp/jackson/gson to a single namespace for the fat jar, or exclude okhttp and rely on the platform artifact. Mixing leads to method-signature mismatches. Example Gradle relocate: `relocate 'okhttp3', 'com.mycompany.relocated.okhttp3'` and do the same for `com.squareup.okio` if needed.

maria: On Jackson vs Gson: NDJSON streaming client used Gson adapters in the SDK but the app depends on Jackson. If both are shaded/relocated inconsistently you can end up with duplicate type adapters or missing serializers for Instant/OffsetDateTime. We had a bug where Instant serializer was provided by shaded-gson but app's Jackson deserializer expected ISO strings and failed.

aj: Huh — that would explain flaky deserialization on the client side. Any practical quick fixes?

yash: Short-term: add a network interceptor to restore Authorization and set `.followRedirects(false)` so you can manually follow redirects and preserve headers. Mid-term: rebuild the client artifact with consistent relocation rules (or publish a thin client without bundled okhttp/gson).

maria: Also check TLS/SNI — proxies doing TLS MITM can rewrite the SNI or cert host which makes the server think it's a different host -> redirect/host mismatch. If you can, test bypassing the proxy (or use `curl --resolve`) to see if SNI is culprit. OkHttp itself supports SNI by default; proxy magic is usually root cause.

leo: For NDJSON streaming fragmentation, make sure `RequestBody` and `ResponseBody.source()` usage is not buffered twice by interceptor; also verify `ConnectionPool` settings and `callTimeout` — aggressive timeouts can cut streams mid-chunk.

aj: Plan: 1) flip to network interceptor re-adding auth + disable automatic redirects to verify; 2) run `jar tf` and `gradle dependencies` to hunt duplicate okhttp/gson/jackson; 3) try thin-client build without shaded okhttp. I'll report results.

maria: 👍 If you post the `jar tf` output I can scan for problematic relocations. Also paste the exact NoSuchMethodError stack.

aj: will do later today. thanks all.

yash: one more: if you keep shading, ensure you relocate `com.fasterxml.jackson` and `com.google.gson` consistently, or exclude one so the app's dependency wins. We added an integration test that runs the fat jar against a local proxy to catch this earlier.

aj: awesome — adding that test to my list. Appreciate the quick pointers :thumbsup:
